doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: First Monday with the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band
summary: After a quartet gig with Thad, Mel gave him the charts in advance; he describes what Mel's drumming meant to the band.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: looking for somebody for the band.” You know and I was like, and I truthfully didn’t know a whole lot about the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band. I knew Thad as a player. I knew his Five by Five, the Monk records that he did and also what he did early on with Mingus, “The Jazz Experiments of Charles Mingus” where you know, so I knew Thad’s playing. I didn’t really know his writing, but I guess I comped in the places that was good — so anyway I had a shot to do the big band and Mel Lewis gave me a heads up on what charts they were doing, so I didn’t have to go in and sight read on a Monday. I had the charts over the weekend or something, and then Mel said we’re going to do this one and we’re not going to do this, don’t worry about that. And he said make sure, look at the ending of this one. So I had a little coaching from Mel. So that was the way I went in on my first Monday and did the big band, and that was a revelation, like now I mean sometimes when I go out to a college and do these Thad Jones charts, I would just try to be the piano player you know. But now I just totally appreciate what Thad, what he did with that band. And you know and it had also to do with Mel, because that whole chemistry of the way Mel played with that band. I played that music with other people, other drummers than Mel. And it’s really like hmm, not quite.
